title: Rubber Hose: An Idea Gets Connected

scenes.title: Night stage wind-up
scenes.purpose: Introduce the bulb character in a spotlight iris on a dark hatched stage and wind up the throw
visuals: Ink field with paper-tone diagonal hatching (stationary)
Bulb crouches (squash) then stretches as both arms whip out on arcs
First cords leave both gloves toward the left and right sockets

beats.development: Anticipation: iris begins opening, bulb squashes down and tucks its arms
Throw: bulb stretches tall, arms swing on arcs to wide poses, glove cords start drawing outward

scenes.title: System connects
scenes.purpose: Show the idea becoming a connected network: sockets pop on as cords reach them
visuals: Landing squash and recovery on planted feet
Sockets pop at uneven times 0.86, 0.97, 1.14, 1.33 s with thinning spark rings
Cords chain socket to socket; the long cord passes under the feet and changes from paper line (outside iris) to ink line (inside)
Pupils glance left then right toward the connections

beats.development: Landing squash; four sockets connect in a staggered, irregular rhythm
Bulb lights: glow rays draw out, single blink, first sparkle twinkles; final cord closes the loop

scenes.title: Wave and settle
scenes.purpose: Reaction pose and a readable settled frame
visuals: Raised arm waves by pivoting at the shoulder; motion marks draw beside the glove
Pose settles at 2.56 s and holds

beats.development: Wave: shoulder pivot up, down, smaller up, then settle; motion marks draw on
Fully settled frame holds for reading the connected system and copy

findings: Primary action (crouch-throw-land) completes by 1.12 s, connections complete by 1.7 s, wave settles at 2.56 s, before the 2.7 s settle requirement
Socket pops are deliberately unevenly spaced so not every object bounces identically
Headline and caption are stationary and legible for the full 3 s
justifiedHolds: 2.56-3.0 s settled hold lets the viewer read the completed network and copy
